extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policymakers, and USCG contracting officers interested in OMB Circular A-76 implementation and cost outcomes
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical analysis of causes for post-award cost increases in OMB Circular A-76 Coast Guard contracts and assessment of USCG perceptions of the A-76 program, including comparisons to the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) and interviews of unit leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of OMB Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 (Contracting out Commercial Activities) ... directs the Government to relay on the private sector for commercial services when evaluated cost is lower in the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This program is the governing policy framework for deciding to contract out commercial activities; an evaluation should determine whether the evaluated (predicted) private-sector cost justified contracting out under A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Labor (DOL) wage determinations as a cause of cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier study of three USCG A-76 contracts showed that Department of Labor (DOL) wage determinations ... caused cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating post-award cost changes, check whether DOL wage determinations (higher wage rates required for contractors) were applied and quantify their impact on contract costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Added work post-award as a cause of cost increases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish increases due to scope expansion or additional tasks from those due to baseline estimation error; document any scope changes and their justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other additional factors causing cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: This thesis analyzed three additional USCG commercial activities to see if DOL wage determinations, added work, or additional factors caused cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and identify additional causal factors beyond wages and added work (e.g., oversight, specifications, transition costs) that may explain post-award cost growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of contract costs with the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract costs were compared with the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) for each activity to see if Government savings were still being realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To assess whether contracting out produced savings, compare actual contract expenditures with the MEO cost baseline and report whether projected government savings persisted after award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting officer actions to control cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: What the Coast Guard contracting officer could do to control them (cost increases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and recommend specific contracting practices, clauses, oversight, or pre-award analyses that contracting officers can implement to limit post-award cost growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of USCG perceptions of A-76 effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: To gauge USCG perceptions of the effectiveness of A-76, interviews were conducted with USCG leaders from units with 'contracted-out' commercial activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure perceived effectiveness via qualitative interviews with leaders in contracted units, and compare those perceptions with leaders from units that retained functions in-house to identify perception differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative interviews (contracted-out vs in-house) to contextualize perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: These [interviews with contracted-out unit leaders] were compared with interviews conducted with leaders from units that had the functions remaining in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paired or comparative qualitative data to discern whether perceptions of A-76 effectiveness correlate with actual contracting outcomes or with whether a unit experienced contracting-out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation problems potentially linked to perceptions of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: There are problems in the implementation of A-76 that may be associated with the perceptions of its effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating program performance, consider implementation issues (e.g., process shortcomings, communication, transition management) as possible drivers of negative perceptions and/or cost outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of updated and expanded sample for assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: This thesis updated the earlier study of three activities and analyzed three additional USCG commercial activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should consider sample size and representativeness; updating prior samples and adding cases helps check whether earlier findings generalize across more activities.
